item.title: ICE agent rebuffed after attempting to enter Ecuadorian consulate in Minneapolis
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS (AP) — Ecuador’s minister of foreign affairs has filed a protest with the U.S. Embassy after Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents tried to enter the Ecuadorian consulate in Minneapolis without permission Tuesday.

item.title: Four charged after hazardous chemicals found near Western University: London police
item.description: LONDON — Four people have been charged after hazardous chemicals capable of being used to make explosives were found in a home near Western University.

item.title: Man wounded after exchanging gunfire with Border Patrol agents near US-Mexico border
item.description: A man who authorities say was involved in a human smuggling operation was shot Tuesday in an exchange of gunfire with the U.S. Border Patrol and after firing at a federal helicopter near the U.S.-Mexico border, authorities said.

item.title: Vigil held in Toronto for man killed by U.S. Border Patrol in Minneapolis
item.description: TORONTO — Dozens of people gathered outside the U.S. Consulate in Toronto on Tuesday for a vigil in memory of Alex Pretti, who was killed by a U.S. Border Patrol officer in Minneapolis on Saturday.

item.title: WADDLING, Carlton Bernard
item.description: Carlton Waddling, known by his wife simply as “Car”, and by his grandkids as “Grandpa Duck”, passed away on January 25, 2026, at Sara Vista Long-Term Care in Elmvale.

item.title: Magnitude 3.7 earthquake gently rocks Southern Ontario
item.description: If it felt like the earth moved beneath your feet late Tuesday night, it did, if you were in Southern Ontario. Earthquakes Canada recorded a magnitude 3.7 quake north of Toronto just before 11:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

item.title: Highway 401 reopened east of Toronto after series of collisions involving 50 vehicles
item.description: A series of collisions involving about 50 vehicles on Tuesday morning forced a prolonged closure of Highway 401 in both directions east of Toronto, Ontario Provincial Police said.

item.title: South Korea's former first lady sentenced to 20 months in prison for corruption
item.description: SEOUL, South Korea (AP) — A South Korean court sentenced former first lady Kim Keon Hee to 20 months in prison for corruption Wednesday ahead of the verdict for disgraced former President Yoon Suk Yeol over his martial law imposition a year ago.
